I will do it the way I usually judge things on my own land. I have only 4.1 mu, so every bag I buy is real money, but if I save too much on fertilizer and the harvest drops, that loss hurts more. So I will start from what has worked before and just keep the field fed a little on the safe side. For wheat, I will use improved seed like most people around me do now, put most of the fertilizer in before sowing, then add nitrogen when the wheat turns green and again when it starts to stand up strong. I have well water, so I will not let wheat go thirsty; I will water about 3 times if the year is normal. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives a better ear if rain and water are enough. I will give maize a bit more nitrogen than wheat, because maize eats strong and fast. I will spray when I see real need, mostly once for weeds and once or twice for insects or leaf disease. I will still plough or rotary till after each crop because on my small land that is the safer way, cleaner and easier for me to manage. If weather is normal, I will aim for a solid harvest, not the highest talk, just what I can really get.
